<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="BRPXQZME" />{{running header|378|{{asc|THE SHIH KING.}}|{{smaller|{{asc|DECADE I.}}}}}}{{rule}}</noinclude>appointment of God came at the proper season.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
King Wăn ascends and descends{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
On the left and the right of God<ref>According to [[Author:Zhu Xi|''K''û Hsî]], the first and last two lines of this stanza are to be taken of the spirit of [[w:King Wen of Zhou|Wăn]] in heaven. Attempts have been made to explain them otherwise, or rather to explain them away. But language could not more expressly intimate the existence of a supreme personal God, and the continued existence of the human spirit.</ref>.

Full of earnest activity was king Wăn,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And his fame is without end.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The gifts (of God) to ''K''âu{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Extend to the descendants of king Wăn{{reconstruct|;—{{lb}}To the descendants of king Wăn|from The Chinese Classics, Vol. IV}},{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
In the direct line and the collateral branches for a hundred generations<ref>The text, literally, is, 'The root and the branches:' the root (and stem) denoting the eldest sons, by the recognised queen, succeeding to the throne; and the branches, the other sons by the queen and concubines. The former would grow up directly from the root; and the latter, the chief nobles of the kingdom, would constitute the branches of the great ''K''âu tree.</ref>.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
All the officers of ''K''âu{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Shall (also) be illustrious from age to age.

They shall be illustrious from age to age,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Zealously and reverently pursuing their plans.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Admirable are the many officers,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Born in this royal kingdom.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The royal kingdom is able to produce them,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The supporters of (the House of) ''K''âu.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Numerous is the array of officers,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And by them king Wăn enjoys his repose.

Profound was king Wăn;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Oh! continuous and bright was his feeling of reverence.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Great is the appointment of Heaven!{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
There were the descendants of (the sovereigns of) {{tooltip|Shang|Shāng}}<ref>The [[Portal:Shang dynasty|Shang or Yin dynasty]] of kings superseded by [[Portal:Zhou dynasty|''K''âu]].</ref>—{{lb}}The
descendants of the sovereigns of Shang{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Were in number more<noinclude><!--¶-->
